newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Cyclone Drena batters New Zealand.
newsitem.headline: Cyclone Drena batters New Zealand.

text.p: New Zealand reeled under its second tropical storm in as many weeks on Friday as Cyclone Drena felled trees, set boats adrift and brought power lines down.
Rain, spring tides and winds of up to 100 km per hour (60 miles an hour) combined to flood parts of Auckland, the country's biggest city.
Power was cut to parts of Auckland for several hours and firemen were called out as roofs were ripped loose by wind and fallen trees.

Inspector Lou Bennett of Auckland police said conditions were "extreme" and police advised drivers of high-sided trucks and light vehicles to stay away from exposed roads and the motorway bridge across Auckland harbour.
Bennett said there had been several reports of motorcyclists being blown into median barriers on the bridge, although no one was seriously hurt.
Coastguards said one yacht was destroyed and five were set adrift in the storm.
However, there were no reports of casualties as Drena headed down the North Island less than two weeks after Cyclone Fergus brought torrential rain and heavy flooding to northern areas.

Both storms have prompted an exodus of holidaymakers from popular northern resorts at the height of summer and some tourist operators have accused weather forecasters of exaggerating their warnings to the public.
